summary: Posaconazole is a broad-spectrum triazole antifungal indicated for prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in severely immunocompromised patients (HSCT recipients with GVHD, prolonged chemotherapy-induced neutropenia). The delayed-release tablet (300 mg loading then 300 mg daily) gives higher, more reliable exposures than the oral suspension and is the preferred oral formulation. Key safety issues are QTc prolongation (with cases of torsades de pointes) and potent CYP3A4 inhibition, which contraindicate co-administration with sirolimus, certain CYP3A4-metabolized statins, ergot alkaloids, pimozide, quinidine, and venetoclax (during ramp-up in CLL/SLL).
indications: Prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in severely immunocompromised patients at high risk (HSCT recipients with GVHD; hematologic malignancy with prolonged neutropenia from chemotherapy)
Indicated in adults and pediatric patients 2 years and older weighing greater than 40 kg (delayed-release tablets)

admin: Swallow delayed-release tablets whole - do not divide, crush, or chew
Administer tablets with or without food (a high-fat meal increases absorption)
Delayed-release tablets and oral suspension are NOT substitutable - follow the specific regimen for each formulation
Delayed-release tablets are preferred over oral suspension for prophylaxis (higher, more consistent exposures)
Obtain a baseline ECG and correct electrolyte disturbances before and during therapy
Review all concomitant drugs for CYP3A4 and QT interactions before starting
moa: Posaconazole is a triazole antifungal that inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51), an enzyme essential for ergosterol biosynthesis. This blocks conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol, disrupting fungal cell-membrane integrity and function, producing fungistatic to fungicidal activity against Aspergillus, Candida, and other moulds. It is also a strong inhibitor of human CYP3A4 and a P-glycoprotein substrate.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to posaconazole or other azole antifungals
Coadministration with sirolimus (sirolimus levels increase ~9-fold; toxicity)
Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates that prolong QT - pimozide, quinidine (risk of QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes)
Coadministration with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 (atorvastatin, lovastatin, simvastatin) - rhabdomyolysis risk
Coadministration with ergot alkaloids (ergotamine, dihydroergotamine) - ergotism
Coadministration with venetoclax at initiation/ramp-up in CLL/SLL - tumor lysis syndrome risk
relative: Potentially proarrhythmic conditions or other QT-prolonging drugs
Hepatic impairment or pre-existing liver disease
Concomitant CYP3A4 substrates (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, midazolam, vincristine) requiring dose reduction/monitoring
Severe diarrhea or vomiting (may reduce absorption and cause breakthrough infection)
monitor: Plasma concentrations of CYP3A4-substrate co-medications (e.g., tacrolimus, cyclosporine, digoxin)

preg: May cause fetal harm based on animal data (skeletal malformations - cranial malformations and missing ribs - and maternal toxicity in rats; increased resorptions in rabbits). Human data are insufficient to establish drug-associated risk. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to the fetus; use only if the benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: There are no data on posaconazole in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or on milk production. Posaconazole is excreted in the milk of lactating rats. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential infant risk.
renal: The pharmacokinetics of the delayed-release tablets are not significantly affected by renal impairment, so no dosage adjustment is necessary for mild to severe renal impairment with oral dosing. Monitor patients with severe renal impairment closely for breakthrough fungal infections. Posaconazole is not removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: Elevations in liver function tests may occur during therapy. Monitor LFTs at baseline and during treatment; consider discontinuation in patients who develop abnormal liver tests attributable to posaconazole. Use with caution in pre-existing hepatic impairment.

major: QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates - pimozide, quinidine: QTc prolongation/torsades de pointes; CONTRAINDICATED
Other QT-prolonging drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 - do not coadminister (additive QT risk)
HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors metabolized by CYP3A4 (atorvastatin, lovastatin, simvastatin) - rhabdomyolysis; CONTRAINDICATED
Venetoclax (CLL/SLL initiation/ramp-up) - tumor lysis syndrome; CONTRAINDICATED at ramp-up (reduce dose otherwise)
Calcineurin inhibitors - tacrolimus (reduce to ~1/3 dose) and cyclosporine (reduce to ~3/4 dose); nephrotoxicity/leukoencephalopathy if levels rise - monitor trough levels
Vincristine and other vinca alkaloids - severe neurotoxicity; reserve azole for patients with no alternative antifungal
moderate: Midazolam and other CYP3A4-metabolized benzodiazepines (alprazolam, triazolam) - prolonged/enhanced sedation (~5-fold midazolam increase); monitor, have reversal available
Digoxin - increased levels; monitor digoxin concentrations
Rifabutin, phenytoin, efavirenz, cimetidine - reduce posaconazole levels; avoid unless benefit outweighs risk
Other CYP3A4 substrates - consider dose adjustment and monitor for toxicity
minor: Fosamprenavir - may lower posaconazole levels; monitor for breakthrough fungal infections
Esomeprazole, metoclopramide - affect oral suspension only (NOT delayed-release tablets)
interactions.food: High-fat meal increases tablet absorption (Cmax +16%, AUC +51%); tablets may be given with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; caution advised given potential for hepatotoxicity
interactions.diagnostics: May cause hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and elevated liver enzymes; monitor ECG for QTc changes

serious: QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes
Calcineurin-inhibitor toxicity (nephrotoxicity, leukoencephalopathy) via raised tacrolimus/cyclosporine levels
Breakthrough invasive fungal infection (with severe diarrhea/vomiting)
emergency: Torsades de pointes / serious ventricular arrhythmia

monitoring: ECG / QTc interval, especially with QT risk factors or interacting drugs
Electrolytes - potassium, magnesium, calcium - before and during therapy
Liver function tests at baseline and periodically
Whole-blood trough levels of tacrolimus or cyclosporine when co-administered
Signs of breakthrough fungal infection, especially with severe GI symptoms or in severe renal impairment
counsel: Swallow the tablets whole - do not crush, chew, or split them
Tablets can be taken with or without food
Tell your doctor about all medicines you take - many serious interactions exist, especially heart-rhythm drugs, statins, transplant drugs, and migraine medicines
Report a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting, or palpitations immediately
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, nausea, or vomiting (possible liver problems)
Report severe diarrhea or vomiting - this can lower drug levels and reduce protection against infection
Do not stop or change other prescribed medicines without telling your doctor
pk: Steady-state plasma concentrations attained by about day 6 at 300 mg (after day 1 loading)
Median Tmax approximately 4-5 hours after an oral dose
Long half-life supports once-daily maintenance dosing after loading
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted to 15-30 C (59-86 F). Child-resistant closure
pearls: Posaconazole prolongs the QTc interval and is a STRONG CYP3A4 inhibitor - screen all co-medications and obtain a baseline ECG; correct electrolytes (K, Mg, Ca) before and during therapy
Delayed-release tablets give higher, more reliable exposures than the oral suspension and are the preferred oral formulation for prophylaxis; the two are NOT interchangeable
Contraindicated with sirolimus, CYP3A4-metabolized statins (simvastatin/lovastatin/atorvastatin), ergot alkaloids, pimozide, quinidine, and venetoclax ramp-up in CLL/SLL
Reduce tacrolimus to ~1/3 and cyclosporine to ~3/4 of original dose and monitor trough levels when starting posaconazole
Pseudoaldosteronism (hypertension + hypokalemia) is a recognized class effect - monitor BP and potassium
Tablet absorption is not meaningfully affected by gastric pH (PPIs/antacids) or renal impairment - unlike the oral suspension
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember. If it is within 12 hours of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the next dose or take more than prescribed.
overdose: There is no specific experience with delayed-release tablet overdose. In trials, oral suspension up to 1600 mg/day and accidental ingestion of 1200 mg twice daily for 3 days produced no adverse reactions different from lower doses. Management is supportive; posaconazole is highly protein bound and is NOT removed by hemodialysis. Monitor ECG/QTc and electrolytes.
